intended_object: The coordinate (Hopf) algebra of the special linear group scheme SL_n over a commutative ring K, i.e. K[x_ij][1/det]/(det − 1), which is isomorphic to K[x_ij]/(det − 1). Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the polynomial presentation equivalence in the same file.
explanation:
The definition is the quotient of `GeneralLinearCoordinateRing.CoordinateRing K n` by the ideal generated by `det(X) − 1`. Here `GeneralLinearCoordinateRing.CoordinateRing K n` is `Localization.Away (det of the generic matrix)` in `MvPolynomial (n × n) K`, the standard coordinate ring of GL_n. So the definition is K[x_ij, det⁻¹]/(det − 1).

This is canonically isomorphic to the textbook presentation K[x_ij]/(det − 1): once det = 1, det is already invertible. The file proves this isomorphism (`polynomialEquiv`). It also proves that the ideal is a Hopf ideal, so the quotient inherits the Hopf structure of SL_n.

Generality: K is any commutative ring and n is any finite type with decidable equality, which is the natural setting for SL_n as an affine group scheme over a base ring. The only restriction is that n must live in the same universe as K. That is a harmless technical choice and does not narrow the mathematics.

Degenerate cases also behave correctly:
- For n empty, det = 1, so the ring is K, the coordinate ring of the trivial group.
- For K the zero ring, the result is the zero ring.

I found no Mathlib definition of the coordinate ring of SL_n or of the group scheme SL_n.
